title: Deployment & Production
blurb: The unglamorous part: APIs, latency budgets, caching, rate limits, secrets, multi-tenancy, cost engineering, the LLMOps stack. This is where AI engineers earn their keep.

nodes.label: API design for LLM products
nodes.description: Streaming vs batch endpoints, idempotency, request schemas, error semantics, versioning. The user-facing contract that has to absorb LLM weirdness.
nodes.doneWhen: You can design a streaming LLM endpoint contract and defend the error-semantics choices.

resources.title: OpenAI API reference (as a design reference)
resources.annotation: Whatever you think of OpenAI, their API is the de-facto reference shape for LLM endpoints. Read it as a design document.

resources.title: Designing Web APIs (Resilient, Performant, Versionable)
resources.author: Brenda Jin et al.
resources.annotation: Not LLM-specific but the right foundation. Versioning, idempotency, error semantics — the parts you'll re-do badly if you skip them.

nodes.label: Latency budgets & SLOs
nodes.description: p50/p95/p99 latency targets, end-to-end budgets, time-to-first-token vs time-to-last-token, SLO/SLA distinctions, error budgets.
nodes.doneWhen: You can set realistic latency SLOs for an LLM feature and decompose them by stage.

resources.title: Google SRE Book — Service Level Objectives
resources.author: Beyer et al. (Google)
resources.annotation: The canonical SRE chapter on SLOs and error budgets. The framing applies directly to LLM endpoints.

resources.title: LLM Inference Performance Engineering: Best Practices
resources.author: Databricks Mosaic AI
resources.annotation: The latency-budget decomposition specific to LLMs: prefill, decode, network, serialization. Read alongside the SRE chapter.

nodes.label: Caching strategies (prompt cache, semantic cache)
nodes.description: Provider-native prompt caching (Anthropic, OpenAI), semantic caching at the application layer, cache invalidation, the safety question of caching personalized output.
nodes.doneWhen: You can pick between prompt caching and semantic caching for a feature and quantify the hit rate.

resources.title: Anthropic prompt caching
resources.annotation: Prefix-based provider caching. The single highest-leverage cost lever for repeated-context workloads.

resources.title: OpenAI prompt caching
resources.annotation: The OpenAI flavor of the same idea. Automatic on long prompts; useful to understand the eligibility rules.

resources.title: GPTCache
resources.annotation: Open-source semantic caching layer. The application-layer answer when prefix-caching doesn't apply.

nodes.label: Rate limiting & fallback
nodes.description: Token-bucket and concurrency limits, model-failover (primary → secondary), graceful degradation, queueing under load.
nodes.doneWhen: You can design a fallback policy that survives a primary-model outage without users noticing.

resources.title: LiteLLM — Fallbacks, retries, timeouts
resources.annotation: The canonical reference for the fallback patterns you'll need. The proxy ships them; the docs explain the choices.

resources.title: Stripe Engineering — Rate limiters
resources.annotation: The clearest explainer of token-bucket and concurrency limiters. Old but the mechanics haven't moved.

nodes.label: Secrets, keys & access control
nodes.description: API key handling, per-tenant keys, BYOK, signing, the on-call horror story of leaked credentials in logs.
nodes.doneWhen: You can audit an LLM service for credential handling and find at least one weakness.

resources.title: OWASP API Security Top 10
resources.annotation: The vendor-neutral baseline for API security. The broken-object-auth and excessive-data-exposure items show up in LLM services routinely.

resources.title: Anthropic — API key best practices
resources.annotation: Vendor-specific guidance but the principles travel: short-lived keys, per-tenant scoping, rotation policy.

nodes.label: Multi-tenant patterns
nodes.description: Per-tenant rate limits, per-tenant model routing, per-tenant evals and cost, isolation. The B2B reality of every AI product company.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe how a multi-tenant LLM platform isolates noisy-neighbor workloads.

resources.title: LiteLLM Proxy — Virtual Keys & Teams
resources.annotation: The pragmatic multi-tenant pattern for LLM access: virtual keys, per-team budgets, model allow-lists.

resources.title: AWS SaaS Lens — Silo, Pool, and Bridge Models
resources.annotation: The canonical silo / pool / bridge taxonomy for SaaS multi-tenancy. Applies to LLM services with minor adjustments.

nodes.label: MLOps / LLMOps
nodes.description: Model registries, prompt registries, dataset versioning, eval-as-CI, blue/green model swaps, the standard ops loop for an LLM product team.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe a basic LLMOps pipeline and identify the difference from classical MLOps.

resources.title: Designing Machine Learning Systems
resources.author: Chip Huyen
resources.annotation: The canonical MLOps reference. The chapters on deployment, monitoring, and infrastructure travel directly to LLMOps.

resources.title: AI Engineering
resources.author: Chip Huyen
resources.annotation: The LLM-specific successor. The chapters on inference, evaluation, and feedback loops are the cleanest treatment of the LLMOps loop.

nodes.label: Cost engineering at scale
nodes.description: Model routing, distillation in production, batch jobs, off-peak inference, the tradeoff curve between cost and quality at scale.
nodes.doneWhen: You can take a $10k/month LLM bill and design a plan to cut it 50% without losing user-visible quality.

resources.title: OpenAI Batch API
resources.annotation: Asynchronous batch at half the cost. The first big lever for any workload that doesn't need sub-minute latency.

resources.title: Anthropic Message Batches
resources.annotation: The Anthropic equivalent. Both APIs are the same architectural choice; familiarity with both lets you route by price.

resources.title: Patterns for Building LLM-based Systems & Products
resources.author: Eugene Yan
resources.annotation: Re-read with the cost lens. The caching and small-model-routing sections are the highest-leverage patterns once you're at scale.

nodes.label: Progressive rollout (canary, feature flags, shadow traffic)
nodes.description: Rolling out a new model or a new prompt without breaking production: feature flags, percentage canary, shadow-traffic comparison, automatic rollback on guard-rail breach. The fast-feedback variant of LLMOps.
nodes.doneWhen: You can design a rollout plan for swapping a prompt or a model and name the metric that would trigger an automatic rollback.

resources.title: Feature Toggles (aka Feature Flags)
resources.author: Pete Hodgson (martinfowler.com)
resources.annotation: The canonical taxonomy of release / experiment / ops / permission toggles. Old but the categorization is exactly right and the LLM use cases map cleanly.

resources.title: Google SRE Workbook — Canarying Releases
resources.annotation: The clearest practitioner-level write-up of canary-rollout design: what to measure, how long to wait, when to fail open vs closed.

resources.title: Deploying Machine Learning Applications in Shadow Mode
resources.author: Christopher Samiullah
resources.annotation: The clearest practitioner write-up of the shadow-mode pattern: mirror traffic to a candidate model, diff the outputs, no user exposure. The fastest way to de-risk a model swap.

nodes.label: Incident response & runbooks
nodes.description: When a model regresses, a vendor outages, a prompt-injection lands, or a cost-spike fires — the on-call discipline that turns chaos into a 90-minute resolution. Severity definitions, runbooks, blameless postmortems, the LLM-specific failure modes.
nodes.doneWhen: You can write a usable runbook for the three most likely failure modes of a deployed LLM feature.

resources.title: Google SRE Book — Managing Incidents
resources.annotation: The reference chapter. Incident command, communication, the difference between IC / OL / CL. The framing applies to LLM ops with no translation.

resources.title: Google SRE Book — Postmortem Culture
resources.annotation: Blameless postmortems, the discipline that turns one outage into a lesson. The bar to aim for, not the bar you'll hit on incident #1.

resources.title: PagerDuty Incident Response documentation
resources.annotation: The open-source-licensed playbook the rest of the industry copies from. Useful as a runnable template when you're standing up on-call for the first time.
